text:
Last night's Integration Debt Night at Kestrelmoor's Flatiron office was one of the more useful panels I've been to this year. About 60 of us showed up to hear how teams deal with the unglamorous work of connecting systems.

The number that stuck with me: Priya Raman-Holt, VP Platform at Tallowbrook, said her team of three engineers maintains 140 partner integrations. Her explanation: "We stopped building connectors one by one and started publishing a spec. Partners build to it now."

Marcus Feldane, founder of Quillary, argued that agent pilots fail at the integration seam, not at the model. His team's rule is to wire up data access before choosing a model.

The room agreed. When asked, about 40 of the 60 said an agent pilot at their company had stalled on getting data access.

The best moment was a disagreement. Priya thinks partners should own their connectors. Marcus thinks the platform has to own them or quality drifts. I left without a clear winner, and I think that's the right place to be.

My takeaway: before the next agent pilot, I'm asking "how will it get the data?" before "which model?"

Thanks to the Kestrelmoor team for hosting.

Where has integration work slowed down your AI plans?
